articles.title: Mbappé hat-trick sinks Real Sociedad after Real Madrid jeered by home fans
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappé scored a hat-trick as Real Madrid beat Real Sociedad 4-1 at the Bernabéu on Wednesday ⁠in their first home match since the return of José Mourinho as head coach.
body: Mbappé put Madrid ahead in the 40th minute before Luka Sucic levelled four minutes later, but the ⁠France forward restored the ⁠hosts’ lead on ​the hour. Vinícius Júnior added a third in the 68th minute before Mbappé completed his treble 10 minutes from time.

It was a winning return ⁠to the Bernabéu for Mourinho, more than 13 years after his previous home match in charge of the club, as Madrid recovered from a disjointed first half ⁠with a ruthless display after the break.
Madrid were jeered before half-time after a sluggish opening in which they ​looked short of rhythm, careless in possession and ‌vulnerable on the counterattack.

“There’s always a sense of justice in the ​boos and the applause, and the odd boo now ‌and then doesn’t do anyone any ‌harm – it helps you grow,” Mourinho said at full time. “We all know the Santiago Bernabéu and just how demanding the fans ‌are here, and I’m very pleased with how my players responded under pressure and put in a great second half, in which we could even have scored more goals.”

articles.title: Chelsea in talks with Martínez’s camp as Aston Villa close on striker Jackson
articles.summary: Blues consider making offer for Argentina goalkeeper. Villa agree £65m Jackson deal as Watkins nears £50m exit. Manchester City expected to make bid for Fernández. Chelsea have been offered Emiliano Martínez and are considering a bid for the goalkeeper.
body: Martínez has told Aston Villa he wants to leave but a move to Juventus collapsed last week after Villa had signed his replacement, Zion Suzuki, from Parma for £30m.

Goalkeeper has been a problematic position for Chelsea in recent seasons, with Robert Sánchez mainly the No 1 but prone to mistakes. Mike Penders, 21, is being lined up to become the first-choice, but the Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso, selected Sánchez for Monday’s win against Fulham when two Sánchez errors led to goals.

The availability and offer of Martínez has intrigued Chelsea and they are mulling whether it is too good an opportunity to turn down. The 33-year-old is a vastly experienced serial trophy winner. He won the World Cup in 2022 and reached the 2026 final. He also lifted the Europa League with Villa last season and the FA Cup with Arsenal in 2020.
Martínez was not in the squad for Villa’s heavy opening-weekend defeat at Brighton. Marco Bizot started in goal with Suzuki on the bench. Martínez joining Chelsea may solve a problem for both clubs.

articles.title: How to follow Thursday's Champions League draw - and who is in each pot?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains when the league phase draw for the 2026-27 Champions League is, as well as looking at who is in each pot
body: The league phase draw for the 2026-27 Champions League campaign takes place on Thursday, 27 August at 17:00 BST in Monaco.
A total of 36 teams will enter that stage of the competition and while 29 teams qualified at the end of last season, the remaining seven places were decided by play-offs.
In the league phase, each team will face eight different teams once, with four home matches and four away matches.

For the draw, the 36 teams will be placed into four pots with one being the highest-ranked and four being the lowest. The pot placements are based on the club's Uefa club coefficient ranking from the five-season period ending at the conclusion of 2025-26.

articles.title: Sávio savours debut goal as Spurs coast to emphatic Carabao Cup win over Charlton
articles.summary: A new season at the snazziest modern stadium in England and something extremely welcome for Tottenham. A home win over domestic opposition. There were only four of them last time out; three in the Premier League with the final one – over Everton on the last day – helping them to avoid relegation.
body: Spurs needed this tonic for another reason – to begin the clean-up operation after Saturday’s awful 3-0 defeat at Brentford.

The season could not have started any worse. With no European football, a decent cup run or runs are imperative and Spurs got themselves up and running in this competition on a night when everything came together perfectly.
For a good while, it looked as though Mikey Moore was going to be the story.
The homegrown 19-year-old broke the deadlock with a vicious drive from the edge of the area; it was the purity of the strike that made it. But then came Sávio.

articles.title: Thierno Barry fires hat-trick as ruthless Everton sweep Preston aside
articles.summary: Thierno Barry resembled a striker reborn, and the goalscorer David Moyes desperately needs, as the first hat-trick of his Everton career plus an assist for new signing Brennan Johnson delivered a resounding win for the Scot on his competitive return to Preston.
body: The France under-21 international scored eight times in a difficult debut season in England but has half that amount two games into this fledgling campaign. Barry followed up his header against Crystal Palace with a poacher’s hat-trick to give Moyes a convincing victory back at the club where he made his name before leaving for Everton in 2002.

“Thierno worked with somebody back home in the summer who tried to change his mindset a bit,” said the Everton manager of the 23-year-old’s early season improvement. “He found it difficult last year, as a lot of boys coming in from overseas do, and it can be even worse if you’re a centre forward. Generally, he has been much better since he came back but I would still like more. A couple of his goals were laid on a plate and I want him to score some of the other opportunities he had as well.”

The Everton manager could not be accused of treating the Carabao Cup lightly on the evidence of his team selection at Deepdale, where only Jarrad Branthwaite and Tyrique George were missing from the side that started on the opening day. Paul Heckingbottom, by contrast, made seven changes from the Preston team beaten by Wolves on Saturday.

articles.title: Newcastle want more new signings after completing Gonzalez deal
articles.summary: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has hailed new signing Nico Gonzalez as a “great addition” and vowed to continue pushing for further reinforcements before the transfer window closes.
body: Gonzalez has joined Newcastle in a £50m deal and the Magpies boss says the club’s recruitment strategy is focused on players like the Spaniard.
“We want to continue our brave way, so not bringing in some guys who almost retire. No, no, this is not our approach,” Jaissle said after his side’s 3-2 Carabao Cup win over West Brom.
“We want to continue that really consistently. So we are bringing a young lad in with Nico, but already an experienced one in the Premier League.
“He has many, many matches and he, like I said, brings a lot of quality in possession, but also physically he’s able to bring impact out of possession.

articles.title: Jed York bodycam arrest video shows stunned 49ers owner’s prostitution bust
articles.summary: NFL owners are in Atlanta, Georgia this week, but San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York is not among them. York ducked this week’s owners’ meeting just days after his bust in East Palestine, Ohio, for engaging in prostitution and possession of criminal tools.
body: York’s charges were ultimately amended to disorderly conduct, but the details have been embarrassing for the billionaire owner.

According to reports, York used the alias “Joe” and contacted a woman on a “known prostitution website” multiple times before he was arrested in a trailer park. York arrived at the agreed-upon location with his $160 ready to go for one hour of sexual acts.
Now, bodycam video of York’s arrest has been released, with the 49ers owner appearing stunned as he was arrested and loaded into a cop car.

York was wearing a New York Yankees T-shirt, basketball shorts, tennis shoes, and his wedding ring while being pulled over in a Volkswagen SUV. York filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle Belluomini, in May 2026 after 15 years of marriage.

articles.title: 'I'm still Will': How UTSA's star running back keeps true to himself
articles.summary: Henderson's fun-loving personality shines through, but he's all business on the field, where he expects to have a big season for UTSA football.
body: A self-described homebody, UTSA running back Will Henderson sometimes makes TikTok videos to fight off boredom. His account has just shy of 1,500 followers, and though the occasional video pops for thousands of views and hundreds of likes, Henderson said he'd be content with much less.
"Just think about, if you get 20 people that like your stuff, that's a lot of likes," Henderson said. "That's 20 people that liked your thing. So, I like seeing that, too."

A little love on social media pales in comparison to the attention Henderson has garnered this offseason. As UTSA's highest-rated and fastest player in the College Football 27 video game, Henderson said he's received plenty of messages thanking him for his contribution to players' dynasties.

His expectations for his real-life performance might be even higher, as Henderson deadpanned that he'd like to rush for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in 2026. His surge late last season has sparked plenty of buzz, putting him in the conversation for various watch lists and preseason all-conference teams.

articles.title: 10 storylines for 2026 high school football season: Can anyone end De La Salle's reign?
articles.summary: Will Pittsburg finally hand De La Salle-Concord its first North Coast Section defeat in 35 years? What about Cardinal Newman-Santa Rosa? Here are the top 10 stories to follow this season.
body: With the 2026 high school football season starting this week - my 43rd consecutive covering the Bay Area and 26th for the Chronicle - here are 10 storylines to follow.

After going 284-0-1 against North Coast Section opponents over the past 35 years - and 33 straight section crowns - the obvious question is, can anyone possibly beat the Spartans? It's truly an age-old quandary with a profound and direct response: no. However, the team to last beat them, the Pirates of Pittsburg (35-27 in the 1991 NCS 3-A finals), has most certainly gained ground, losing by single scores the last three meetings (30-23, 10-7 and 24-17).

With former longtime defensive coordinator Charlie Ramirez in his fourth season as head coach, a Division I college prospect quarterback in junior JaVale Jones and a boatload of future college players led by speedy junior receiver Kenneth Ward, edge rusher Terrance Murphy (Fresno State) and two-way playmaker Isaiah Harrison, the Pirates appear equipped to pull off the seemingly impossible. More importantly, playing the Spartans to the final horn in the playoffs recently, there is an internal belief they can slay the dragon.

articles.title: Barry hat-trick helps Everton saunter past Preston
articles.summary: Thierno Barry scored three goals and set up the other as Everton sauntered into the third round of the Carabao Cup by way of a 4-0 win over Preston at Deepdale.
body: The French striker scored eight goals in 41 games in 2025/26 and, after his first of the season in Saturday's Premier League win over Crystal Palace, is now already halfway to matching that total despite having played 38 games fewer.
The Toffees - who have not progressed past the third round since 2023/24 - have been drawn to face Wolves in the next round.

A strong Everton team were in control from the off. They dominated the ball and chances came thick and fast against a Preston side who've lost two from two in the Sky Bet Championship but, for the most part, those openings were of low quality.
The 10th attempt was a successful one. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's floated ball released Vitalii Mykolenko on the left, who laid the ball on a plate for Barry to sweep in a tidy finish.

articles.title: Humphries out to deny Littler historic clean sweep after winning PC28
articles.summary: Luke Humphries beat Brendan Dolan in the final to win his third Players Championship title of the season on the second day of action in Leicester.
body: Luke Humphries wins on the second day of Players Championship action in Leicester after 8-6 victory over Brendan Dolan, who had beaten Luke Littler in semi-final; Littler, who made his first two appearances of 2026's series this week, with work to do if he is to make November finals.

Humphries, who reclaimed the world No 2 position in the PDC rankings from Gian van Veen during the course of the day, beat Ireland's Dolan 8-6 to win PC28 for his first title in the series since PC17 in May, also held at the Mattioli Arena.
Dolan had defeated Luke Littler 7-4 in their semi-final to deny the world No 1 a blockbuster meeting with Humphries.
Humphries beat Mike De Decker 7-4 in his semi-final, two rounds after surviving six match darts against Danny Noppert to win that match 6-5.
